Sasha: Heads up — after yesterday's KV cache TTL change I see per-route tokens in Console are lower than the ledger by ~120k tokens for a handful of tenants. Console UI shows normal; invoices show the higher number. Anyone else seeing this?
Emilia: Which deploy/commit? can you paste an example tenant and the queries you ran?
Sasha: It was the kv-cache-ttl bump to 20s rolled at 02:00 UTC. tenant: tb-04f7. Console query I ran: 
```sql
SELECT sum(tokens) FROM route_breakdown WHERE tenant='tb-04f7' AND day='2026-03-20';
```
Ledger query returns ~122400 more tokens for same day.
Raj: Could be late-session merges — events arriving after the aggregation watermark get applied into ledger replays but not into the first-pass Console aggregates. Does ingest show late-arrival flags? @ingest-bot
ingest-bot: ingest-bot: Found 246 late events for tenant tb-04f7 between 02:01-02:15 UTC; marked with `arrival_latency_ms > 60000`.
Marta: We changed the TTL used for prefix merging; that reduction could reduce prefix coalescing and make short sessions emit more granular events which then get re-joined later. Need raw event ids to trace. Sasha, can you share 2–3 event ids?
Sasha: Pasting sample ids: evt_aea12, evt_aeb34, evt_afc56
Also pulling logs: `kubectl -n metering logs deploy/ingest-consumer | grep evt_aea12` — shows the event was first seen at 02:02:12 and then reprocessed at 02:07:01 during a downstream retry.
Alex: If late events are reprocessed into the ledger while Console only shows first-pass aggregates, we have two choices: backfill Console aggregates or emit explicit "adjustment" events so invoices show a correction line. UX: negative/retroactive lines look scary on invoices.
Emilia: I like the explicit correction event approach. Add `event_type = 'recon_adjustment'` and emit signed token deltas (positive or negative) with a `causal_event_id`. Then Console can surface them separately and invoices can render them as "adjustments" not new charges. This needs an event-bus schema bump.
Raj: Schema change is fine but safety first — avoid double-charges if a replay and original both land. Implementation idea: when ingest detects `arrival_latency > X` and the event falls outside the agg-window, write an `adjustment` event with `token_delta = actual_tokens - deduped_tokens` (signed). Ledger will sum deltas; invoice renderer treats `adjustment` as correction.
Marta: Operationally, keep this behind a feature-flag at routing/ingest so Dedicated customers can opt-out. Canary plan: staging -> 5% prod -> 50% -> global. Also add telemetry: gauge for `adjustment_tokens/sec` and per-tenant adjustment volume so SRE/CS can triage billing noise.
Sasha: I'll open an RFC and collect a few affected tenants for verification. Also propose a one-off backfill that takes late events we already know about and emits `recon_adjustment` so the current invoice aligns with Console for those customers.
Alex: I'll prototype the schema + a small consumer change. Quick sketch: 
```json
{ "event_type":"adjustment", "tenant_id":"tb-04f7", "token_delta":122400, "causal_event_id":"evt_aea12", "reason":"late_arrival" }
```
Emilia: :thumbsup: Action items: Sasha (investigate sample tenants & file RFC), Alex (schema prototype + consumer patch), Raj (safety checks + replay strategy), Marta (canary + dashboard metrics). I'll update the rollout doc with the flag gating.
ingest-bot: ingest-bot: Created ticket MET-4931: "retro-adjust events and console align" and attached logs (internal link).
